item_verdicts.title: Fiedler accumulator core (clamp, NaN/negative guards, drift-free stepping) — in place; the RESUME_HERE '250 inline' backlog row is stale
item_verdicts.why: Source verified: gafferongames.com/post/fix_your_timestep/ is live and contains the accumulator loop, the `if (frameTime > 0.25) frameTime = 0.25` clamp (=250ms), and the interpolation recipe. Repo verified: Sim.advance (src/core/Sim.ts) rejects NaN and negative deltas, clamps via Math.min(deltaMs, MAX_FRAME_MS), and computes owed frames multiplicatively from total elapsedMs with FRAME_QUANT_EPS (src/config/timing.ts, documented as the 1-ulp guard). MAX_FRAME_MS = 250 lives in src/config/combat-sim.ts labeled Spec-fixed and is imported by Sim.ts and src/game/fidelity.ts. Grep finds no inline 250 and no scene-side accumulator anywhere in src/game/ (DuelScene just calls sim.advance(delta × timeScale)), so the RESUME_HERE 'Spark / backlog' row (line ~200-201) describing the inline-250 replacement is indeed already satisfied — stale as claimed.

item_verdicts.title: Render interpolation of fighter motion: canon says always, the OG measurably says NEVER — a fidelity DIVERGENCE here
item_verdicts.why: The core survives every attack: ledger §S24-E partb says verbatim that 'the 60 fps burst proves the snap lands wholly between two ADJACENT 1/60 s frames (pure 15 fps stepper, zero interpolation)', and neither the §00b corrections table nor §S24-H overturns it (§S24-H actually cites §S24-E as RESOLVING Contradiction #3). src/config/anim.ts has OG_ANIM.poseStepMs = 1000/15 with the comment '0 = smooth (veto)', exactly as adjudicated. But the source attribution contains a fabricated quote: simplified.media never says interpolation is 'nearly always necessary' — I fetched the page twice; its only 'almost always' sentence describes the accumulator REMAINDER ('there is almost always a small remainder'), not the technique. The page does still recommend interpolation universally ('The remedy is interpolation'; 'Usually yes…'; no omission cases named), so the substance of the canon-vs-OG contrast stands.
item_verdicts.correction: Replace the simplified.media source annotation "claims interpolation 'nearly always necessary'" with: "recommends interpolation universally ('The remedy is interpolation'; names no case where it should be omitted) — its 'almost always' phrase describes the accumulator remainder, not the technique." The REJECT adjudication and §S24-E citation are unchanged.

item_verdicts.title: The real gap is the OPPOSITE of canon: fighter render POSITION is still 60Hz-smooth while the pose latches at 15fps
item_verdicts.why: Every repo and ledger fact checks out. drawFighters (src/game/DuelScene.ts) computes worldToStage(player.pos)/worldToStage(enemy.pos) fresh on every rAF update with no positional latch, while the pose is latched through OgAnimPlayer at OG_ANIM.poseStepMs — so positions do glide at sim rate between 15fps poses, exactly the asymmetry claimed. Ledger §S24-E partb says verbatim: constant-speed line-follow '18–22 world px per 15 fps tick' with a 'GENUINE alternating ~27/55 px two-tick stride… (recreate it, don't average it)', plus the terminal contact snap, and explicitly flags that 'the current DASH_SPEED_PX_PER_FRAME (≈2400 world px/s continuous)… mismatch the measured ~276–330 world px/s line-follow + snap — A12.2 input'. Sim.ts does move dash/move positions every 60Hz tick (tick() steps speedPxS/FIXED_HZ). Both cited sources are live and support their attributed points (Fiedler: render sampling decoupled from sim; docs.phaser.io TimeStep: step fires at rAF cadence). One honest caveat for the implementer, not a refutation: §S24-H lists the adversarial verify of the §S24-D/E numbers as '[VERDICT PENDING]', so the 27/55 and 18–22 figures are first-pass measurements not yet skeptic-confirmed.

item_verdicts.title: visibilitychange / backgrounded-tab handling — covered by three cooperating layers; no missing canon
item_verdicts.why: Sources verified: MDN rAF page says verbatim that calls 'are paused in most browsers when running in background tabs or hidden iframes'; the Phaser 3.60 Timestep changelog URL is live (mentions the new smoothDelta method), and docs.phaser.io/api-documentation/class/core-timestep independently confirms smoothStep default TRUE ('enabled in Phaser 3 since the first version') and that pause() is called 'when the visibility API says the game is hidden'. Repo verified: Sim.advance clamps every call to MAX_FRAME_MS=250 (a resume's giant delta arrives as one call and is capped at 250ms of sim time), and src/game/DuelIntro.ts update() contains both the quoted comment ('the original Flash game simply paused when hidden') and the re-anchor (stepAt += now − lastNow when the gap exceeds 500ms). ALREADY_DONE holds. Minor nit only: the smoothStep-default-true specific is documented on the TimeStep API page, not on the cited 3.60 changelog page itself.

item_verdicts.title: 144Hz / high-refresh displays — correct by construction; the canon 'fix' (interpolation) is moot below the 66.7ms content quantum
item_verdicts.why: MDN verified verbatim: callback frequency 'will generally match the display refresh rate… 75hz, 120hz, and 144hz are also widely used', plus the warning that without elapsed-time math 'the animation will run faster on high refresh-rate screens'. Repo verified: Sim.advance accumulates clamped wall-clock elapsedMs and derives owed 60Hz frames from the cumulative total, so sim speed is refresh-rate independent by construction — a 144Hz rAF simply yields 0-or-1-tick advances. The mootness argument holds against the repo: the drawn pose is latched to OG_ANIM.poseStepMs = 1000/15 ≈ 66.7ms (src/config/anim.ts), coarser than any 60/144Hz beat. The proposed action is a no-code eyeball VERIFY, so nothing here can regress the sim.

item_verdicts.title: Interpolation's only possibly-legitimate scope — camera parallax and HUD meter fills — needs a frame-diff measurement before any smooth tween is added
item_verdicts.why: Every ledger citation checks out at the row level: §00 says verbatim 'This is a property of the archival capture, not necessarily of the Flash game (which likely ran 24–30 fps)'; §S24-E says '60 fps bursts show exact 4-duplicate-frame content blocks'; §S24-G trap 9 names the A28 boulder layer parallaxing at 0.73× (with the mushroom cluster as a fake static anchor — a real hazard the proposed measurement must dodge); advanceFxClock exists and drives the fx tween clock in src/game/DuelScene.ts. None of these rows appear in the §00b or §S24-H corrections. The MEASURE_FIRST adjudication is the honest reading of the §00-vs-§S24-E tension — note only that §00's byte-identical evidence is cited for the nameplate REGION (e.g. video A f164–167), so 'whole-frame 15Hz render' is inference, which is precisely why measuring pans and HP-bar windows before latching camera/HUD is the right call.

overall_note: The research output survives adversarial review almost intact: 5 CONFIRMED, 1 WEAKENED, 0 REFUTED. All five fetched sources are live and support their attributed claims, with two nits: (1) simplified.media's 'nearly always necessary' is a fabricated quote — the phrase describes the accumulator remainder, though the page does recommend interpolation universally, so item 2's REJECT stands on the ledger + anim.ts veto comment as it says it does; (2) item 4's smoothStep-default-true fact lives on the TimeStep API doc page, not the cited 3.60 changelog. Repo checks all pass: Sim.advance (clamp/NaN/negative/multiplicative owed frames + FRAME_QUANT_EPS), MAX_FRAME_MS=250 Spec-fixed in src/config/combat-sim.ts, no inline 250 or scene accumulator left (backlog row genuinely stale), drawFighters position-per-rAF vs pose-latched asymmetry real, DuelIntro re-anchor comment real. Ledger checks pass: §S24-E partb quotes verbatim, untouched by §00b/§S24-H corrections. One standing caveat for the ADAPT item: §S24-H records the adversarial verify of the §S24-D/E numbers as '[VERDICT PENDING]', so the 27/55-px stride and 18–22 px/tick figures driving A12.2 are first-pass measurements — worth closing that verdict before hard-coding them.
